- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

45	// Tier-B restore: stage vl in rs1 and vtype in rs2 via Abstract Commands,

48	{

2	// regfile transfer. The Debug Module abstract-command space has no slots for
3	// v0..v31 (the RISC-V Debug Spec leaves V to the Program Buffer or
4	// implementation-specific extensions), so vsim moves v0..v31 by executing a
5	// vle8.v/vse8.v sweep on the halted hart through the Program Buffer (see
6	// pb_v_data_sweep in program_buffer.hpp, driven by ResumeDriver on resume and
7	// StateDrain at drain). That sweep loads/stores the V scratch region of guest
8	// RAM -- the top page of the mapped span (v_scratch_gpa, L26); this header

11	//   - stage_v_to_scratch: state.vreg[] -> scratch RAM, called before resume so
12	//     the ResumeDriver vle8.v sweep reads QEMU 1's V values.

37	// Total scratch bytes needed: 32 V regs × HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX. Sized to the
38	// maximum supported VLEN; the actual per-reg byte count is `vlenb`. Defined in
39	// the shared ABI (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES) so the driver's mmap sizing and this
40	// consumer agree on one count (L26/F2).
41	inline constexpr std::size_t kVScratchBytes = HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES;

43	// L26: the scratch region is the TOP kVScratchBytes of the mapped RAM span,
44	// not a fixed address. Scheme D parks it just above the program's declared
45	// RAM (the driver maps one page more than --mem-size), so no program layout

47	// address the Program-Buffer sweep (ResumeDriver/StateDrain) loads/stores
48	// through; the host stager below copies span-relative and needs no base.
49	inline constexpr auto v_scratch_gpa(uint64_t ram_base, std::size_t ram_size)
50	  -> uint64_t

52	  return ram_base + static_cast<uint64_t>(ram_size) - kVScratchBytes;

58	// (loud) rather than silently transporting V through a bogus address.

66	// if the span is smaller than one scratch page (a too-small RAM mapping).
67	inline auto scratch_offset(std::size_t ram_size) -> std::size_t
68	{

77	// Walk every transported Andes+M-ext CSR in canonical order -- Andes scalars,
78	// PMA ADDR, PMA CFG, then M-ext -- gated by the live block flag AND engine
79	// caps. Invokes fn(csr_addr, field_ref) per transported CSR. State is
80	// templated so it binds const (enumerate) and mutable (populate). PMA addr
81	// precedes cfg because the restore's TOR/NAPOT cfg consumes the addr already
82	// in place (mirrors the PMP/PMA restore ordering). Applies the same `(flags &
83	// FLAG) && caps.supports_csr(addr)` predicate every consumer of the block
84	// uses, so the single X-macro keeps them in lockstep.
85	template<typename State, typename Fn>
86	inline void for_each_transport_csr(State& state, const AndesCaps& caps, Fn&& fn)
87	{
88	  if (state.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES) {
89	#define X(field, addr, name) \
90	  if (caps.supports_csr(addr)) fn(uint16_t(addr), state.andes.field);
91	    HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)
92	#undef X
93	    for (int p = 0; p < HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM; ++p)
94	      if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR + p))
95	        fn(uint16_t(HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR + p), state.andes.pmaaddr[p]);
96	    for (int p = 0; p < HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM; ++p)
97	      if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR + 2 * p))
98	        fn(uint16_t(HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR + 2 * p), state.andes.pmacfg[p]);
99	  }
100	  if (state.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT) {
101	#define X(field, addr, name) \
102	  if (caps.supports_csr(addr)) fn(uint16_t(addr), state.m_ext.field);
103	    HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(X)
104	#undef X
105	  }

109	// resumes the hart so the fixture can vle8.v from scratch and pick up QEMU 1's
110	// V values.
111	inline void stage_v_to_scratch(const hybrid_state_v1& state,
112	                               std::span<uint8_t> ram)
113	{
114	  const auto off = detail::scratch_offset(ram.size());
115	  // Pack at vlenb stride (drop the wire-format padding) so v0..v31 sit
116	  // contiguously and the Program-Buffer sweep can move 8 at a time via LMUL=8.
117	  const std::size_t vlenb = state.vlenb;
118	  for (std::size_t r = 0; r < 32; ++r)
119	    std::memcpy(ram.data() + off + r * vlenb,
120	                state.vreg + r * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX, vlenb);
121	}

124	// drain path after the fixture's prologue vse8.v has settled the (possibly
125	// mutated) regfile bytes into RAM.
126	inline void read_v_from_scratch(hybrid_state_v1& state,
127	                                std::span<const uint8_t> ram)
128	{
129	  const auto off = detail::scratch_offset(ram.size());
130	  // Unpack the vlenb-packed scratch back into the wire-strided vreg[] slots.
131	  // Each slot's padding (bytes vlenb..HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX) is left as-is:
132	  // callers pass a passthrough state whose padding is already zero (the QEMU
133	  // drain zero-fills it), so the full 128-byte slots stay byte-identical to the
134	  // oracle that --verify compares against.
135	  const std::size_t vlenb = state.vlenb;
136	  for (std::size_t r = 0; r < 32; ++r)
137	    std::memcpy(state.vreg + r * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX,
138	                ram.data() + off + r * vlenb, vlenb);

`ResumeDriver` (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) writes every CSR row in this
table -- the base M-mode scalars, the Andes V5 block, and the M-ext block --
with one Abstract Command per CSR, gated by the LG1 liveness check. There is
no Program-Buffer CSR sweep: a `csrrw` to a caps-supported but read-only /
WARL-illegal CSR raises `cmderr`, and a batched Program-Buffer program can't
recover from a fault partway through without corrupting the rest of the
batch, whereas the abstract path's per-CSR `clear_cmderr` just tolerates
that one CSR and moves on to the next. `StateDrain` mirrors the policy: one
abstract read per CSR. GPRs and FPRs likewise restore and drain via one
Abstract Command per register.

The Program Buffer carries only the state the abstract command space cannot
reach: the V data-register sweep, V's `vtype`/`vl` Tier-B `vsetvl`, and the
L2C MMIO window.

92 ROADMAP.md
# ROADMAP: liveness-gated transport (hybrid resume/drain)

Goal: stop paying Debug-Module traffic for state the program never changed.
Motivating profile (rt_c_hello, hybrid, --drain-minimal, ax45mpv_premium):
the vsim leg simulates 50,448 cycles for a 54-cycle ROI at ~9.8 kHz (5.2 s
wall). Split: Andes CSR block 15,235 cy / floor 13,334 cy / M-ext CSR block
9,622 cy / V transport 6,959 cy / FPR block 5,298 cy. Each DM operation
(abstract command or PB exec) costs ~200-900 simulated cycles.

Mechanism: compare each drained value against the ENGINE's own reset value
(a `hybrid_state_v1` baseline drained from the engine at reset). Equal means
the write is a no-op -- skip it. This is verify-transparent by construction
and self-heals QEMU-vs-engine reset divergence (msp_bound, milmb, ...).
mstatus-liveness (FS/VS == Off) was measured useless for C programs: hello
drains FS=Initial, VS=Clean with all-zero FPR/V data.

Known-limit notes:
- The DRAIN-side CSR sweep is ON (full drains only; minimal drains skip it).
  It needed the caps map exact: two over-claims faulted a batched csrr on
  premium and are fixed -- mcountermask_m 0x7D1 (UMODE-gated now, was
  PERF_MONITOR) and jvt 0x017 (new ZCMT gate, was CODENSE). A faulting batch
  is bisected so the error names the offending CSR. No baseline interaction:
  the liveness gate elides RESTORES only.
- The RESTORE-side CSR sweep stays OFF (a csrrw can fault on read-only/WARL
  fields); if ever enabled, filter its addr list by the baseline first (it
  would bypass the gate).
- Write-order hazards (mcounterwen gating counter writes) exist today in the
  tolerant path and are neither fixed nor worsened by gating; tracked by the
  separate caps/ordering audit.

## Features

### LG1: baseline-gated tolerant CSR restore -- state: DONE
- Description: `ResumeDriver::set_reset_baseline(state)` + skip every
  `write_csr_tolerant` call site (9 base scalars, Andes X-list, PMA loops,
  M-ext X-list) whose value equals the baseline. Never gated: mstatus, dpc,
  GPRs, mcycle, minstret, dcsr, S/U PMP mirror. `baseline_skip_count()`
  exposes the elision count for tests/logs. Dormant until LG3 wires a
  baseline in.
- Key files: `src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`,
  `tests/hybrid/resume_driver.test.cpp`.
- Dependencies: none.

### LG2: baseline-gated FPR / V block skip -- state: DONE
- Description: skip the whole FPR fld-sweep + fcsr when fpr[0..31]+fcsr all
  equal the baseline; skip V staging + vle-sweep + vsetvl + vstart/vxsat/
  vxrm/vcsr when vreg bytes + V CSRs all equal the baseline. Decide whether
  the S/U PMP mirror joins the gate. Host-side staging (memcpy into scratch)
  may stay unconditional -- scratch is transport-only.
- Key files: `src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`, `src/simulator.hpp` (staging),
  `tests/hybrid/resume_driver.test.cpp`.
- Dependencies: LG1 (shares baseline plumbing + skip counter).

### LG3: reset-baseline capture + cache -- state: DONE
- Landed notes: cache key adds the ELF identity (the hart free-runs a few
  workload insns before the DMI halt, so the halted state is per-ELF);
  capture enables mstatus.FS/VS first (reset leaves them Off and the
  fsd/vse8 capture sweeps fault otherwise); capture runs pass
  v_cfg_at_reset=false (the capture V sweep clobbers vtype/vl/vstart).
- Description: at hybrid resume the hart is freshly reset and halted -- the
  first run per engine build drains that reset state via StateDrain (~43k cy,
  one time), saves it under $XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/reset-<engine>-<version>
  .bin (validate magic/version + engine identity on load), and feeds it to
  ResumeDriver on every later run. `--no-reset-baseline` escape hatch.
  spdlog: cache hit/miss + skipped-write count.
- Key files: new `src/hybrid/reset_baseline.hpp` (key/path/load/save, unit-
  testable), `src/simulator.hpp` (`apply_resume_from_qemu`), `src/main.cpp`
  (flag), `tests/hybrid/reset_baseline.test.cpp`.
- Dependencies: LG1, LG2.

### LG4: e2e proof + docs (andesim repo) -- state: DONE
- Landed notes: full suite green with the gate live and a cold cache
  (47/47: marker 23, pc 23, neg 1); `--verify` PASS (146 fields);

  location; andesim CLAUDE.md ResumeDriver bullet updated.

1	// Andes-CSR capability gating.
2	//
3	// A core implements an Andes custom CSR only when the matching feature is
4	// configured into it (config.inc). Restoring a CSR the target core lacks can
5	// hang the DMI handshake -- observed on ax45mpv_premium for ucode (no DSP) and
6	// mecc_code (no ECC). So the resume/drain loops transport only the CSRs the
7	// target core supports, decided here from the core's feature gates.
8	//
9	// This header is Verilator/SystemC-free: it maps a CSR address to its gate and
10	// answers "does a core with these gates support this CSR". The binding of each
11	// gate to the core's compiled-in `_NDS_*` config macros lives in the sim binary
12	// (see andes_caps_from_config), so this stays unit-testable in isolation.
13	#ifndef ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP
14	#define ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP
15	
16	#include <cstdint>
17	#include <string>
18	#include <vector>

24	// The hardware feature that gates each transported CSR. ALWAYS = unconditionally
25	// present (a base machine CSR every core has; never gated off). The first block
26	// gates the v3 Andes custom CSRs; the second block (UMODE..TRIGGER) gates the v4
27	// M-ext CSRs (HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST) -- standard + Andes M-mode CSRs whose
28	// existence depends on a privilege level or extension the core may not have.
29	enum class AndesGate : uint8_t {
30	  ALWAYS = 0,
31	  DSP,
32	  CODENSE,
33	  ZCMT,        // standard Zcmt table jump (jvt); NOT implied by CoDense
34	  POWERBRAKE,
35	  STACKSAFE,
36	  ECC,
37	  PMA,
38	  ILM,
39	  DLM,
40	  PERF_MONITOR,
41	  // The Andes PMNDS counter scheme (SPA: mmsc_cfg.PMNDS). RTL ground truth
42	  // (kv_csr_dec.v existent_csr): these CSRs exist iff PERFORMANCE_MONITOR
43	  // AND NOT SSCOFPMF -- a core with the standard Sscofpmf count-overflow
44	  // extension REPLACES the Andes scheme. The _UMODE/_SMODE variants add the
45	  // privilege term the spec conditions carry (PMNDS & misa[20] / misa[18]).
46	  PMNDS,        // Andes-scheme perf counters (perf monitor && !Sscofpmf)
47	  PMNDS_UMODE,  // PMNDS && U-mode
48	  PMNDS_SMODE,  // PMNDS && S-mode
49	  ALT_FP,       // umisc_ctl: spec ALT_FP_FMT|CST_CTL, RTL BF16_ARITH|ACE
50	  // v4 M-ext gates.
51	  UMODE,       // needs U-mode  (NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2)
52	  SMODE,       // needs S-mode  (NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS == 3)
53	  EPMP,        // ePMP / Smepmp (mseccfg)
54	  SMRNMI,      // resumable NMI (mnscratch/mnepc/mncause/mnstatus/mnvec/mrnxvec)
55	  EXCSLVL,     // exception save levels (msave*)
56	  CLIC,        // CLIC / enhanced CLIC (mtvt/mintthresh/mcirq_entry)
57	  SMSTATEEN,   // state-enable (mstateen0..3)
58	  CCTL,        // cache control CSRs (mcctlbeginaddr/mcctldata)
59	  PPI,         // private peripheral interface base (mppib)
60	  FIO,         // fast IO base (mfiob)
61	  TRIGGER,     // debug triggers (tselect/tdata1/tdata2/tcontrol/mcontext)
62	};

64	// Map an Andes CSR (by address) to the feature gate that enables it. Addresses
65	// are the HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST scalars plus the PMA block. A CSR with no
66	// custom-extension gate is ALWAYS (a base machine CSR every Andes core has).
67	// Maintainer note: a CSR added to HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST that needs gating must
68	// get a case here, else it defaults to ALWAYS (transported unconditionally).
69	constexpr AndesGate andes_gate_for(uint16_t csr_addr)
70	{
71	  switch (csr_addr) {
72	    case 0x801: return AndesGate::DSP;           // ucode (DSP overflow flag)
73	    case 0x800: return AndesGate::CODENSE;        // uitb  (CoDense table base)
74	    // jvt is Zcmt's table-jump base, NOT part of classic CoDense (exec.it +
75	    // uitb): a CoDense core without Zcmt faults a csrr of it (seen on
76	    // ax45mpv_premium, where it aborted the drain CSR sweep).
77	    case 0x017: return AndesGate::ZCMT;           // jvt   (Zcmt only)
78	    case 0x7C5: return AndesGate::POWERBRAKE;     // mpft_ctl
79	    case 0x7C2: return AndesGate::ECC;            // mecc_code
80	    case 0x7C6:                                   // mhsp_ctl
81	    case 0x7C7:                                   // msp_bound
82	    case 0x7C8: return AndesGate::STACKSAFE;      // msp_base
83	    case 0x7C0: return AndesGate::ILM;            // milmb (ILM base)
84	    case 0x7C1: return AndesGate::DLM;            // mdlmb (DLM base)
85	    // v4 M-ext CSR gates (HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST).
86	    // The PMNDS counter block (SPA existence: mmsc_cfg.PMNDS, plus misa[20]
87	    // or misa[18] for the U/S members). Over-claiming any of these faults a
88	    // PB csrr with cmderr=3, aborting a CSR sweep -- seen live for 0x7D1 on
89	    // premium (M-only) and 0x7CF on advanced (Sscofpmf replaces PMNDS).
90	    case 0x7CF: return AndesGate::PMNDS;          // mcounterinten
91	    case 0x7CE: case 0x7D1: case 0x7D3:           // mcounterwen, mcountermask_m/_u
92	      return AndesGate::PMNDS_UMODE;
93	    case 0x7D2: return AndesGate::PMNDS_SMODE;    // mcountermask_s
94	    case 0x30A: case 0x306:                       // menvcfg, mcounteren
95	    case 0x808: case 0x80B: case 0x811:           // uzobctl, ucctlbeginaddr, sleepvalue
96	      return AndesGate::UMODE;
97	    // umisc_ctl: "Access Mode: User and above" is WHO may touch it, not an
98	    // existence condition -- spec existence is ALT_FP_FMT | CST_CTL (RTL:
99	    // BFLOAT16_ARITH | ACE, no privilege term). The UMODE gate under-claimed
100	    // it on both (M-only) engines; found by the registration audit.
101	    case 0x813: return AndesGate::ALT_FP;
102	    case 0x7D5: return AndesGate::SMODE;          // mslideleg
103	    case 0x747: return AndesGate::EPMP;           // mseccfg
104	    // The STANDARD counters exist under either perf-monitor scheme (Zihpm);
105	    // only the Andes PMNDS block above is scheme-dependent.
106	    case 0x320: case 0xB03: case 0xB04: case 0xB05: case 0xB06:  // mcountinhibit, mhpmcounter3-6
107	    case 0x323: case 0x324: case 0x325: case 0x326:              // mhpmevent3-6
108	      return AndesGate::PERF_MONITOR;
109	    case 0x740: case 0x741: case 0x742: case 0x744:  // mnscratch, mnepc, mncause, mnstatus
110	    case 0x7DE:                                       // mrnxvec
111	      return AndesGate::SMRNMI;
112	    // mnvec is base Andes NMI state -- spec "IM Requirement: Required", RTL
113	    // decodes it unconditionally on cores that lack Smrnmi entirely. It was
114	    // wrongly grouped with the Smrnmi CSRs and under-claimed on every engine.
115	    case 0x7C3:                                   // mnvec
116	    case 0x7C9: return AndesGate::ALWAYS;         // mdcause (base Andes trap CSR)
117	    case 0x7D6: case 0x7D7: case 0x7D8: case 0x7D9:  // msavestatus, msaveepc1, msavecause1, msaveepc2
118	    case 0x7DA: case 0x7DB: case 0x7DC:              // msavecause2, msavedcause1, msavedcause2
119	      return AndesGate::EXCSLVL;
120	    case 0x307: case 0x347: case 0x7EC:           // mtvt, mintthresh, mcirq_entry
121	      return AndesGate::CLIC;
122	    case 0x30C: case 0x30D: case 0x30E: case 0x30F:  // mstateen0..3
123	      return AndesGate::SMSTATEEN;
124	    case 0x7CB: case 0x7CD: return AndesGate::CCTL;  // mcctlbeginaddr, mcctldata
125	    case 0x7F0: return AndesGate::PPI;            // mppib
126	    case 0x7F1: return AndesGate::FIO;            // mfiob
127	    case 0x7A0: case 0x7A1: case 0x7A2: case 0x7A5: case 0x7A8:  // tselect, tdata1, tdata2, tcontrol, mcontext
128	      return AndesGate::TRIGGER;
129	    default:
130	      // PMA cfg (0xBC0, 0xBC2) and addr (0xBD0..0xBDF) blocks.
131	      if (csr_addr == HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR || csr_addr == HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR + 2)
132	        return AndesGate::PMA;
133	      if (csr_addr >= HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR &&
134	          csr_addr < HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR + HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM)
135	        return AndesGate::PMA;
136	      return AndesGate::ALWAYS;                    // mxstatus 0x7C4, mclk_ctl 0x7DF
137	  }
138	}

140	// The set of Andes feature gates a target core has on. Built from the core's
141	// compiled-in config (config.inc) in the sim binary and injected into the
142	// resume/drain loops, so they transport only the CSRs the core implements.
143	// Default = every gate on (all(): no gating, the prior unconditional behavior).
144	struct AndesCaps {
145	  uint32_t gate_mask = ~0u;
146	
147	  static constexpr AndesCaps all()  { return AndesCaps{~0u}; }
148	  static constexpr AndesCaps none() { return AndesCaps{0u}; }
149	
150	  constexpr void set(AndesGate g, bool on = true)
151	  {
152	    const uint32_t bit = 1u << static_cast<unsigned>(g);
153	    if (on) gate_mask |= bit;
154	    else    gate_mask &= ~bit;
155	  }
156	
157	  constexpr bool gate_on(AndesGate g) const
158	  {
159	    return (gate_mask >> static_cast<unsigned>(g)) & 1u;
160	  }
161	
162	  // ALWAYS-gated CSRs are present on every core regardless of the mask.
163	  constexpr bool supports_csr(uint16_t csr_addr) const
164	  {
165	    const AndesGate g = andes_gate_for(csr_addr);
166	    return g == AndesGate::ALWAYS || gate_on(g);
167	  }
168	};
169	
170	// F6: build the caps from the CSR addresses the registered manifest transports,
171	// instead of from config macros (andes_caps_from_config). The transported set is
172	// a union of COMPLETE gate-groups -- supports_csr() keys on the gate, so every
173	// CSR sharing a gate transports together -- hence setting each transported CSR's
174	// gate reconstructs the EXACT caps. This lets the runtime be driven by the
175	// measured/registered manifest, making the config->caps model (the andesim
176	// mirror + parity guard) redundant. Verilator-free, so it stays unit-testable.
177	inline AndesCaps andes_caps_from_transport_set(const std::vector<uint16_t>& transported)
178	{
179	  AndesCaps c = AndesCaps::none();
180	  for (const uint16_t addr : transported)
181	    c.set(andes_gate_for(addr), true);
182	  return c;
183	}
184	
185	// The gated CSR names this core supports, for the --describe card. Iterates the
186	// two single-source-of-truth X-macro lists: the v3 Andes custom CSRs and the v4
187	// M-ext CSRs. The driver uses this list to gate --verify, so a CSR the core
188	// lacks is neither restored, drained, nor compared.
189	inline std::vector<std::string> supported_andes_csr_names(const AndesCaps& caps)
190	{
191	  std::vector<std::string> out;
192	#define X(field, addr, name) if (caps.supports_csr(addr)) out.push_back(name);
193	  HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)
194	#undef X
195	  // PMA group markers (whole pmacfg[]/pmaaddr[] blocks share one gate), so a
196	  // consumer can include/exclude PMA without listing all 18 entries.
197	  if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR))  out.push_back("pmacfg");
198	  if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR)) out.push_back("pmaaddr");
199	  // v4 M-ext CSRs share the same address->gate map and --describe list.
200	#define X(field, addr, name) if (caps.supports_csr(addr)) out.push_back(name);
201	  HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(X)
202	#undef X
203	  return out;
204	}

# Makefile to build libaceasim.a for different CPU versions
# Usage: make INCDIR=path/to/your/include all
# Or you can do `make 45` or `make 46` to build specific version
# the built binary is like 45/libaceasim.a

VERSIONS := $(patsubst %/,%,$(wildcard */))
TARGETS := $(addsuffix /libaceasim.a,$(VERSIONS))

all: $(TARGETS)

INCDIR ?=

	for lib in $(filter %.a,$^); do ar x $$lib --output=$*; done; \

ver.o: ver.c
